what_happened: The the person running Athena used the kill switch on job kjy2. That job was a plain retry of 9h6z, which had just hit the 3000s producer deadline, and it kept the same scope. The the person running Athena judged it would very likely time out again, cost about $3 and 50 minutes, and stop the drain. They re-asked the work as vbee, narrowed to one timed run, fixing only the biggest cause, with at most two full test runs. The job class is prompts.
cause: Retry does not check why the previous attempt failed. After a producer deadline, Athena queues the same scope again with the same fixed deadline, and nothing narrows the scope, warns that a repeat is likely to fail, or holds it. The producer also gives no progress signal or partial result to show which part of the work is expensive. Only the the person running Athena's judgment stopped a predictable repeat failure.
prevention: When a job failed on a producer deadline, make retry and auto-requeue refuse an identical-scope attempt. Require either a narrowed reading (one timed run, a single cause, a cap on full test runs) or an explicit the person running Athena override. Hold the retry and show the previous deadline, the spend, and the expected cost. Also record the producer's partial progress at the deadline, so the narrowed retry can start from the biggest known cause.
proposed_request: Change retry handling so that a job whose last attempt ended on the producer deadline cannot be retried or requeued at the same scope. Outcome: such a retry is held with a message naming the earlier deadline, its cost and the cost expected for the retry. It proceeds only if the reading is narrowed (a single cause, one timed run, at most two full test runs) or the the person running Athena explicitly overrides. Acceptance: (1) a test where a job failed on the producer deadline shows an identical-scope retry is held, not started; (2) a narrowed retry is accepted; (3) an explicit override is accepted and logged as an intervention; (4) the held message shows the deadline, the spend so far and the expected cost; (5) a held retry does not stop the drain from running other items.
